idiom_name: defaultdict(list) of callables keyed by topic
implementation_notes: Python has no stdlib pub-sub primitive; the local idiom is a plain registry - a defaultdict(list) or dict keyed by event type, whose publish() iterates a snapshot of the list and calls each callable. The classic channel class collapses into a dozen lines, so hand-writing it is usually justified only when the unsubscribe token, thread safety and error policy are made explicit. Iterate over a copy so subscribers can unsubscribe from inside a callback.
pitfalls: Iterating the live subscriber list while a callback unsubscribes raises RuntimeError or skips subscribers; snapshot with list() and decide the exception policy per subscriber.
A registry of bound methods holds strong references and keeps the subscriber alive for the channel's lifetime; store weakref.WeakMethod or require explicit unsubscribe.
Without a lock, subscribe/publish from multiple threads can lose registrations or mutate the mapping during iteration.

variants.name: blinker named signals
variants.implementation_notes: blinker packages the registry behind named global signals: signal('name') returns the same signal object anywhere in the process, connect() registers receivers (optionally scoped to a specific sender, optionally weak), and send() fans out and collects return values; send_async() supports coroutine receivers. Take it when signals must be shared across modules without passing a channel object (Flask's signals are blinker), at the cost of implicit global names.
variants.code_sketch:
from blinker import signal

order_placed = signal('order-placed')
order_placed.connect(billing.handle, weak=True)   # receiver auto-disconnects
result = order_placed.send(shop, order_id='o-1')  # every receiver is invoked
order_placed.disconnect(billing.handle)
pitfalls: Named signals are process-global: any module can connect to a name, so a publisher cannot see its audience at the call site.
signal('x') always returns the same object; receivers connected in tests leak into later tests unless disconnected or muted.
Weakly connected receivers disappear silently once nothing else holds the bound method - a lost subscription looks like a bug in the publisher.
